target: For every prime p>3, S_p = sum_{n=0}^{p-1}(6n+1) C(2n,n)^2 C(3n,n)/216^n ≡ p*(-3/p) (mod p^3).

sun_a14_ii.reference: Zhi-Wei Sun, Open Conjectures on Congruences, arXiv:0911.5665, Conjecture A14(ii)
sun_a14_ii.specialization: a=1 is exactly the present target after multiplying the displayed normalized congruence by p.

beukers.reference: Frits Beukers, Supercongruences using modular forms, arXiv:2403.03301 (current revised version audited 2026-08-27)
beukers.specialization_status: Coefficient family and CM value t=sqrt(-6)/3 -> 1/216 match exactly; Theorem 1.22 has the required F_p-delta^{-1} theta F_p shape but assumes p splits in Q(sqrt(-6)). Numerical q-expansion gives delta=-1/6, but this audit does not promote the numerical identification or the theorem character sign to an exact standalone specialization.

shvets_2026.reference: Alex Shvets, Split-prime supercongruence at the mixed CM point (1/6,1/3;1), arXiv:2605.19773
shvets_2026.specialization_status: Uses the same mixed (1/6,1/3) hypergeometric CM backbone after Clausen, but proves a symmetric-cube coefficient congruence rather than the derivative-weighted p-term truncation here; not a closure.

exact_matches: Its level-3 CM point alpha=sqrt(-6)/3 has t(alpha)=1/216.
The weighted operator would match F_p+6 theta F_p if delta(alpha)=-1/6.
lane_a_modular_cm.scope_obstruction: Theorem 1.22 requires p split in Q(sqrt(-6)); for p>3 this excludes p ≡ 13,17,19,23 (mod 24).
lane_a_modular_cm.nonproof_check: Independent high-precision q-expansion audit gave delta(alpha)=-1/6, but an exact symbolic derivation and exact character identification were not completed, so no restricted-class theorem is claimed by this return.

lane_b_direct_padic.consequence: Only the last third vanishes termwise modulo p^3. The two middle layers survive at p and p^2 precision and must be controlled.

smallest_unresolved_frontier.name: INERT_FINITE_CLAUSEN_DERIVATIVE_BRIDGE
smallest_unresolved_frontier.statement: For primes p inert in Q(sqrt(-6)), control modulo p^3 the difference between the degree-(p-1) truncation of (1+6 theta) _3F_2 at z=1/2 and the p-adic Frobenius/Clausen expression built from _2F_1(1/6,1/3;1;z), including the valuation-1 and valuation-2 middle blocks.
smallest_unresolved_frontier.why_it_is_smallest: The exact formal Clausen identity handles coefficients below degree p, while evaluation of the truncated square introduces degree >=p convolution tails; these are precisely where the surviving middle p-adic layers must be accounted for.

recommended_next_action: Attack the inert finite-Clausen derivative bridge directly using a p-deformed terminating hypergeometric/WZ identity or p-adic Gamma expansion. Do not spend another stage merely extending finite prime bounds or re-citing split-prime modular theorems.
